32 What is the definition of the potential difference (p.d.) across a component?
A
the electrical power supplied to the component
B
the energy transferred to the component per unit charge
C
the product of the current in the component and its resistance
D
the voltage across the component

hints: Notice the question asks for the definition of p.d. across a component, not a formula that can be used to calculate it in a special case.
Recall that p.d. links energy transferred $W$ in joules to charge $Q$ in coulombs passing through the component.
Compare energy per unit time with energy per unit charge, and check whether $V = IR$ or the word voltage actually defines the meaning of $V$.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the meaning of potential difference across a component through which charge flows and energy is transferred.
State the governing definition: p.d. is work done or energy transferred per unit charge, $V = W/Q$, with unit $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$.
Check the other statements: power is $P = W/t = VI$ in watts, so electrical power is energy per second, not per coulomb.
Check $V = IR$: this product of current and resistance gives the p.d. for a metallic conductor at constant temperature, but it does not define what p.d. means for every component.
Check voltage: saying p.d. is the voltage only gives an alternative name and does not state the energy-per-charge idea.
Therefore only the energy transferred to the component per unit charge matches the definition. This is option B.

A.explanation: Power is energy per unit time, $P = VI$, not energy per unit charge, so this confuses p.d. with rate of transfer.

B.explanation: This is the definition $V = W/Q$, where $W$ is energy transferred in joules and $Q$ is charge in coulombs.

C.explanation: The relation $V = IR$ is true for a resistor obeying Ohm's law but it is a consequence, not the definition of p.d.

D.explanation: Voltage is another name for p.d., so this restates the term without defining it as energy per charge.
